English translation:
1 [...]
1 [...] from the city of Oxyrhynchus. Since
2 Theon son of Pausiris, of
3 the same city of Oxyrhynchus, has served on me through the
4 strategus of the nome a copy of a memorandum, which he im-
5 properly had executed at the record office,
6 by which he made a demand for what he alleged
7 to be owed to him both by the maternal grandfather of my minor son
8 Sarapion, Sarapion,
9 and his brother Dionysius, from former
10 times, as capital sums of silver, I make the
11 proper counter-statement, declaring that I suspect that the security
12 of the loan which he claims to have existed has been discharged,
13 both because it is of long standing and because
14 Sarapion survived two years, and after his death
15 his daughter, who became my wife
16 and mother of the minor Sarapion, Eubu-
17 lia, likewise survived eleven years, and
18 after her death too another five years
19 passed, and Theon did not venture
20 to come forward; and further that Eubulia,
21 while she was alive, sold to the aforesaid
22 brother of Sarapion, Dionysius, property
23 of Sarapion for six talents of silver
24 and more, on condition that he should pay
25 Sarapion's creditors the debts owed by him,
26 and that Theon, being creditor of Sarapion for other
27 capital sums, recovered those
28 from Dionysius, but made no mention at all
29 of this one. Therefore I ask you to give orders to write to the strategus of the Oxyrhyn-
30 chite nome to serve on Theon a copy
31 of this memorandum, so that he may know
32 that the notice which he improperly served on me
33 is void, and to serve also whatever he may write in reply,
34 while my right to legal action against
35 him remains in matters where it is needed, I contenting
36 myself with this declaration, as is proper. Year 15
37 of Imperator Caesar Trajanus Hadrianus
38 Augustus, Epeiph 1. Signed, Epeiph 1.

Loan in ll. 6-12.
Date: about 18 years before the petition (AD 131): Sarapion lived 2 years after the loan, Eubulia 11 more, then 5 more years passed.
Place: not stated; the place of the document.

English translation:
1 ⳨ To my good master, lover of Christ, lover of the poor, all-
2 renowned, most magnificent patrician and dux of the Thebaid
3 region, Apion, from Anoup, your wretched slave, from the
4 estate belonging to it called Phakra.
5 The glorious house of my good master possesses nothing unjust or impious,
6 but is always full of mercy, pouring out to the needy
7 what they need. Therefore I too, the wretched slave of my good master,
8 through this present petition wish to be shown mercy,
9 (and) to make known to your lordship that from my fathers and forefathers I have served
10 my good master, paying the public taxes every year; and by God's
11 will, in the past eleventh indiction and the past
12 tenth my animals died, and I borrowed no little gold,
13 (15 solidi), until I could buy the same animals. But when I approached
14 my good master and (asked him) to have mercy on me, (and) came here, the agents
15 of my master would not consent to act according to the order of my good
16 master. For if, master, your mercy does not reach me, I cannot stand
17 on my holding and be useful to the landowner's affairs. And
18 I beseech and implore your lordship to order that mercy be shown
19 to me, since I have come to great ruin. For I have no other
20 refuge but that of the Lord Christ and of your eminence.
21 And I will send up undying hymns to the Lord Christ for the
22 life of your lordship and of its most magnificent son
23 Strategius, master. ⳨

Loan in ll. 11-13.
Date: after the animals died in the 10th and 11th indictions (AD 546-548), before the petition (AD 548/9?).

English translation:
(recto)
1 ⳨ In the reign of our most divine and most pious master Flavius Justinian, eternal Augustus
2 and Imperator, year 24, in the 8th (year) after the consulship of Flavius Basilius, vir clarissimus,
3 Phaophi 22, indiction 14, in the city of Oxyrhynchus. ⳨
4 To Flavius Apion, the all-renowned and most magnificent former consul ordinarius,
5 landowner also here in the splendid city of the Oxyrhynchites, through Menas, servant, who makes the stipulation
6 and acquires for his own master, the same all-renowned man, the right of action and
7 obligation, the community of the protokometai of the village of Takona of the Oxyrhynchite
8 nome, whose pagarchy is held by the house of your glory, through us, the Aurelii
9 Phoebammon, meizon, son of Pekysius, and Anoup son of Aritsi, and Menas his brother,
10 and Koulaetb son of Iohannes, and Anoup son of Priscus, and Heraclides son of Palmas, and Phib son of
11 Iulius, and the other komarchs of this (village), greeting. We acknowledge that we have received from
12 your glory as a loan, and have had measured out to us from the produce of the present
13 fourteenth indiction, for the sowing of our arouras for the crops of the
14 fifteenth indiction, with God's help, of uncleaned wheat, without the sifting allowance,
15 by the cancellus measure, two hundred artabas, which were also given to us through the heirs of the
16 late Menas son of Asclas, shipmaster of your same glorious house, total 200 artabas of wheat by the cancellus measure;
17 which wheat, new and sifted, by the cancellus measure by which we received it, we will of necessity
18 return to your glory, together with our rent, in the month of Payni
19 of the present year 227 (and) 196, of the same present fourteenth indiction,
20 from the new crops of the fifteenth indiction, with God's help, without delay, at the risk of
21 our property, which is pledged for this. The document, written in a single copy, is valid, and in answer to the formal question we have acknowledged it. ⳨
22 We, the community of the protokometai of the village of Takona of the Oxyrhynchite nome, through the aforesaid
23 persons named in it, (have made) this document to your glory, and (have received) the wheat, two hundred artabas,
24 uncleaned, without the sifting allowance, by the cancellus measure, total 200 artabas of uncleaned wheat, and we will return it at the stated term,
25 and all that is written is agreeable to us as aforesaid, ⳨ and in answer to the formal question we have acknowledged
26 and ἀπελήσαμεν (meaning unclear). I, Aurelius Heraclides, scribe of the village of Takona, having been asked, wrote for them,
27 as they are illiterate. ⳨
28 ☧ Executed through me, Philoxenus. Phaophi 23, indiction 14 [...] ⳨
(verso)
29 ⳨ Document made by the protokometai of the village of Takona
30 for the sowing of the crops of the 15th indiction, 200 artabas of wheat by the cancellus measure.

Loan in ll. 11-21; Menas is the brother of Anoup son of Aritsi.
Date: Phaophi 22, indiction 14, year 24 of Justinian (= 19 October AD 550).
